subject: Parallax - Order Form & Output / Training License: proposed compromise
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@parallax.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@parallax.com, tom.rivera@parallax.com
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Parallax MSA redlines + output/training concerns

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Parallax is excited about Redwood. Our legal team attached an MSA redline and a proposed Order Form. Two points they flagged that we need clarified before we can move to procurement:

1) Output ownership: we want explicit assignment of customer-generated output (search results, generated copy) so downstream productization is unambiguous.
2) Training & feedback: we cannot allow our production data or outputs to be used to train Redwood models for model improvement unless we opt in and receive clear provenance & deletion controls.

I've attached the redline (Parallax_MSA_Redline_20261118.docx) and OrderForm_Parallax_20261118.pdf. Can Redwood legal propose an alternative that addresses our IP/feedback concerns while keeping your hosted offering workable?

Best,
Alice Chen
Head of Legal, Parallax Systems

Alice — thanks for the redlines and for surfacing the two concerns. Looping in Karthik (legal) and Monica (account lead) so we can propose a clean path forward.

Quick ask from our side: can you confirm whether Parallax considers the generated output to be proprietary code/unique content that requires exclusive assignment, or whether you need license/attribution for downstream commercial use? That distinction will shape our proposed clause.

PRI: next steps — Karthik and I will review and respond with a track-changes proposal by EOD tomorrow. Monica, can you ready the procurement contact details and any PO timeline?

Thanks,

From: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, monica.patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@parallax.com>
Date: 2026-11-19T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Parallax MSA redlines + output/training concerns

Thanks, Priyom & Alice. I reviewed the redline. Summary of legal's position and a compromise path below.

Summary:
- We are comfortable assigning a broad, perpetual, worldwide license to customer-generated output for customers to use/redistribute internally and commercially (nonexclusive). We do not typically assign title for outputs that are derived from our hosted model service because our infrastructure and underlying model weights are not transferred.
- Regarding training: Redwood's default is to treat customer data and outputs as non-training unless a customer expressly opts in via an Order Form checkbox. Parallax's redline requests a categorical prohibition on training and use of outputs for model improvement. We can accept that in principle but need operational controls and evidence if you want a hard prohibition.

Proposed compromise (to put in track-changes):
1) Output license: Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, transferable, worldwide, irrevocable license to use, modify, and exploit Customer-Provided Prompts and Customer-Generated Output ("Customer Output") for any purpose, subject to standard confidentiality and export controls. Redwood will not assert ownership of Customer Output.

2) Training & feedback: by default, Redwood will not use Customer-Provided Content or Customer Output to train Redwood models for product improvements. If Customer wants Redwood to use their data for training, an explicit Training Opt-In (Order Form checkbox + scope) is required, together with controls: data segregation, deletion window, and proof-of-consumption reports.

3) Telemetry & safety data: Redwood may collect aggregate telemetry (latency, token counts, error rates) and low-fidelity safety signals for service quality; these will be non-identifying and not used to improve model semantics.

4) Evidence & audit: Redwood will provide an annual attestation and on-demand proof (within reason) that Customer data was excluded from training pipelines if Customer has selected the opt-out. This may be subject to redaction for system secrets.

Monica — if Parallax needs stronger contractual remedies (e.g., liquidated damages, injunctive relief) for training violations we can discuss escalation to Commercial Ops, but our standard approach is the opt-in model and attestation/audit hooks.

Alice — can you confirm whether this addresses Parallax's ask, or if they need title assignment (rather than license) for Customer Output? If they insist on title we will escalate to Policy & Product — that path can slow timelines.

Karthik Iyer
Deputy Counsel, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@parallax.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: monica.patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, legal@parallax.com, tom.rivera@parallax.com
Date: 2026-11-19T13:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Parallax MSA redlines + output/training concerns

Karthik — thanks for the thoughtful proposal. Two clarifications from Parallax legal:

1) License vs Title: Parallax strongly prefers assignment of title for machine-generated outputs that are unique to our prompts (examples: finely tuned marketing copy variants, generated code templates). The ask is to avoid any ambiguity for downstream monetization. If Redwood's platform produces uniquely attributable creative that Parallax invested to create, we need title.

2) Attestation: the attestation/audit approach is promising. We need (a) quarterly attestation while terms are in force and (b) an on-site or third-party audit right once annually (subject to NDA).

If Redwood cannot accept title assignment, Parallax is willing to accept an exclusive, perpetual license with the same economic scope as assignment plus the audit and injunctive remedies.

If you can update the doc to reflect the alternative license that is exclusivity-limited to outputs derived solely from Parallax prompts (and to include the quarterly attestation + annual audit right), we can route to procurement.

Best,
Alice
attachments: none

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@parallax.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, monica.patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-20T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Parallax MSA redlines + output/training concerns — next steps

Alice — appreciate the flexibility. Proposed operational next steps to keep momentum:

1) Redwood will prepare two tracked drafts by tomorrow morning: (A) assignment-lite: perpetual, exclusive license limited to Customer-Generated Output derived solely from Customer prompts; (B) assignment-exit: a title assignment path that requires product-level approvals and a 6–8 week policy/product review.

2) Audit/attestation: we will accept quarterly attestations and an annual third-party audit right under NDA. Legal will add standard scope limitations (no access to raw model weights, redaction of Redwood confidential syslogs).

3) Training opt-in UI: ask Parallax whether they want (a) a single-order-form checkbox for all environments, or (b) per-environment toggles (prod vs sandbox). That will affect implementation timing.

Monica — please capture Parallax procurement cadence and whether they need a PO or formal SOW to lock timelines. Alice — if this plan sounds acceptable we will post the two drafts to the shared Drive link and request a short legal sync (30 minutes) to finalize.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this.
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
